trial.title: SAPIEN M3 EFS: Early Feasibility Study of the Edwards SAPIEN M3 System for the Treatment of Mitral Regurgitation

endpoints.time_frame: At the end of the procedure
endpoints.description:
Defined as meeting all the following:

* Alive
* Successful access, delivery and retrieval of the delivery systems
* Deployment of the devices in the intended position
* Freedom from emergency surgery or reintervention related to the device or access procedure

outcome.rationale: Early feasibility study design focuses on safety and technical performance rather than comparative efficacy. Based on TMVR class evidence and device-specific abstract reports, SAPIEN M3 is likely to demonstrate acceptable technical success and MR reduction to support continued development. Single-group design without control limits definitive efficacy claims but feasibility endpoints appear achievable

value.uncertainty: Limited direct SAPIEN M3 evidence; estimate based on TMVR class data (85-95% technical success typical in EFS) with uncertainty for dock-deployment-specific challenges
value.rationale: TMVR early feasibility studies typically achieve 85-95% technical success. SAPIEN M3 dock-based deployment adds complexity but abstract reports suggest feasibility. Conservative 85% estimate accounting for anatomical screening challenges in high-risk MR population

analysis_trace.trial_identification: NCT03230747: Early Feasibility Study of Edwards SAPIEN M3 System for Mitral Regurgitation (n=72, single-group, high-surgical-risk patients)
analysis_trace.indication: Severe mitral regurgitation (MR ≥3+) in high-risk surgical patients
analysis_trace.patient_population: Adults ≥18 years with severe MR, NYHA ≥II, high surgical risk, EF ≥30%, excluding those with prohibitive anatomy or recent cardiac events
analysis_trace.target_mechanism: Transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) using SAPIEN M3 valve and dock system
analysis_trace.endpoint_interpretation: Primary (primary-0): Technical Success (composite of alive, successful access/delivery/retrieval, correct deployment, no emergency surgery). Secondary (secondary-0): MR reduction to grade 0-1+ at 30 days
analysis_trace.safety_analysis: Key safety concerns: LVOT obstruction, device embolization, access complications, bleeding. TMVR procedures carry inherent risks but early feasibility studies typically show manageable safety profiles
analysis_trace.key_risks: Anatomical unsuitability for dock deployment, LVOT obstruction, paravalvular leak, device migration, procedural mortality
analysis_trace.evidence_to_prediction: Evidence from search results indicates TMVR early feasibility studies (Intrepid, AltaValve) typically report technical success rates 85-95% and MR reduction rates >85%. SAPIEN M3-specific evidence from 2019 TCT abstract (JACC 2019) reported updated 30-day outcomes. Evidence role: indirect_direction for TMVR category; mechanism_background for SAPIEN M3 specific outcomes. No direct numeric results retrieved due to source unavailability.
analysis_trace.coverage_gaps: Direct SAPIEN M3 EFS results not retrievable. Cannot confirm exact technical success or MR reduction rates. Evidence relies on class-level TMVR data and device-specific abstracts without full numeric extraction
analysis_trace.major_uncertainties: Exact technical success rate for SAPIEN M3 dock deployment mechanism unknown. Patient-specific anatomical screening and LVOT obstruction risk assessment variability affects predictions
